obtained.how: agency copy: the U.S. EPA Region 1 administrative-record copy (Merrimack Station NPDES record, AR-783) of the USFWS report, served from EPA's 19 January 2017 web snapshot; the scan carries the National Wetlands Research Center library stamp

bibliography.checked_against: the title page (PDF p. 4) and the report's own 'should be cited as' line (PDF p. 5)
bibliography.note: 'Aho, J. M., C. S. Anderson, and J. W. Terrell. 1986. Habitat suitability index models and instream flow suitability curves: redbreast sunfish. U.S. Fish Wildl. Serv. Biol. Rep. 82(10.119). 23 pp.' (November 1986) — matches

claims.claim: mature at age II, most fish beyond age III spawn (southern studies, via Aho, Anderson & Terrell 1986)
claims.location: p. 1 (PDF p. 10), Age, Growth, and Food
claims.quote: first observed at age II; most individuals older than age III are reproductively active
claims.conditions: a literature statement citing Davis 1972, Bass & Hitt 1974, Sandow et al. 1974 and Carlander 1977
claims.note: 'most individuals older than age III' — i.e. age IV and older. The passage does not give the studies' localities; elsewhere the report cites Bass & Hitt 1974 for 'southeastern coastal plain habitats', so 'southern studies' is a fair gloss but not stated here

claims.location: p. 1 (PDF p. 10), Age, Growth, and Food
claims.quote: as 8 years, but the average life span appears to be between 4 to 5
claims.conditions: literature statement, no population or locality given

claims.quote: anticipated to be closer to the approximate value of 36°C reported for largemouth bass
claims.conditions: an inference from largemouth bass, not a redbreast measurement; the report says redbreast temperature preference and CTmax 'are not well known for any life history stage'; redbreast have been observed at 33–35 °C in thermally impacted Savannah River Plant reservoirs

claims.quote: temperatures of 25-30 °C should result in maximum growth, survival, and reproduction
claims.conditions: inferred from preferenda of largemouth bass (27–29 °C) and green sunfish (28 °C), not measured on redbreast; reduced growth and survival expected below 15 °C or above 33 °C
claims.note: the report's own caveat is worth keeping: preferenda are assumed to approximate largemouth bass rather than bluegill (29–31 °C)

notes: All four uses hold; all are literature statements or inferences in an HSI model, mostly from southeastern populations. Other useful values (p. 1–3, PDF pp. 10–12): redbreast are generalist invertivores, adults ≥ 101 mm take more terrestrial insects; spawning peaks at 20–25 °C (21.0–25.0 °C in Davis 1972), apparently once a summer; colonial nests 30–60 cm apart in < 1.5 m of water near hard structure on sand/gravel; deep water used for overwintering (Breder & Nigrelli 1935); DO below 1.0 mg/L lethal on prolonged exposure (assumed as for bluegill, Moore 1942); found at pH near 4.0.
